faqs.question: Our child gets home at 4:30pm and finishes homework near 8pm. When does tuition even fit?
faqs.answer: Usually in one of two places, and it is worth choosing deliberately. Either a short weekday slot immediately after the break, around 5:30pm, taken before homework rather than after it, or a longer weekend morning session with only a brief midweek check-in. The pattern that fails most often on this road is an 8pm or 8:30pm weekday start, because the student is finished by then and retention drops sharply. Tell the advisor the real timings rather than the ideal ones, and the shortlist will be built around slots that can actually hold.

faqs.question: Is grade 9 in IGCSE the same as Grade 9 in school?
faqs.answer: No, and the overlap in wording causes real confusion. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and Cambridge's 9 to 1 syllabuses report results on a numerical scale where 9 is the highest grade, above the old A star, down to 1 at the bottom. Grade 9 in school is the first of the two IGCSE years, with exams normally sat at the end of Grade 10. So a Grade 9 student is not sitting for a grade 9. Some Cambridge syllabuses still report A star to G, which is why families see both systems in the same conversation.

faqs.question: Can a tutor take two students from different flats in the same society?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and it is worth asking about in towers like Vatika City, Tata Primanti or Central Park Resorts. A tutor already teaching inside your complex can offer consecutive slots without any travel between them, which makes their timings more reliable and their weekday availability wider. It also means a missed session is easier to reschedule. Group sessions are a separate question and depend on whether both students are on the same board, tier and roughly the same point in the syllabus, which is less common than parents expect. Availability is subject to tutor schedules.

faqs.question: My child scored 62 percent on a past paper. What grade is that?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which paper and which series. Grade boundaries are set after each examination series based on how the cohort performed and how demanding that particular paper was, so the same raw percentage can land on different grades in different years. Marking a paper properly means using that paper's own mark scheme and boundary table, not a general percentage rule. Any tutor who converts a raw score into a confident predicted grade without checking the boundary table for that series is giving you a guess dressed up as an assessment.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE English need a tutor if my child already reads a lot?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, because reading widely and answering to a mark scheme are different skills. Cambridge 0500 Paper 2 asks for directed writing in a specified form with a specified audience, and strong readers routinely lose marks by writing an essay where a speech or a letter was required. Reading paper questions also reward precise short answers over elaborate ones. If your school follows the Edexcel English Language A coursework route instead, the work is spread differently across the two years. A few sessions on format and mark scheme often does more than months of general reading.

faqs.question: How does online tuition handle marking and homework properly?
faqs.answer: Reasonably well when the tutor insists on it. The workable pattern is that the student photographs or scans handwritten work and sends it before the session, the tutor marks against the official scheme, and the session is spent on the errors rather than on watching the student write. Screen sharing suits graph work, apparatus diagrams and step-by-step algebra. What does not survive online is unsupervised timed practice, so timed papers are better sat at home under a parent's eye and reviewed in the session afterwards.

faqs.question: We may move from Sohna Road to Golf Course Extension Road mid-year. Does the tutor change?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Tutors working the Sector 65 to 68 side already cover both corridors, so a home arrangement often survives the move with a timing adjustment. If the tutor is based on the older side near Sector 47 or 48, the journey may stop being practical, and converting to online is usually simpler than starting over with someone new mid-syllabus. Raise the move a few weeks ahead rather than after it happens, because continuity with the same tutor through Grade 10 is worth more than a marginally shorter commute.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with school coursework without doing it for the student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary should be stated at the start. Legitimate support is teaching the underlying content, explaining what the assessment criteria reward, reviewing a plan, and giving feedback on a draft the student wrote. What is not acceptable is a tutor writing, rewriting or dictating coursework, which is a malpractice issue for the student and the school, not a grey area. Ask any prospective tutor how they handle drafts. A clear answer about feedback rather than authorship is a good sign about how they will work generally.

faqs.question: What happens if we see no improvement after two months?
faqs.answer: Two months is long enough to expect a diagnosis at minimum, even if marks have not moved. Ask the tutor for a written list of topics now secure, topics still weak, and what the student has attempted unaided. If that list cannot be produced, the sessions are not being planned and a change is warranted. If it can be produced and shows real progress that has not yet reached a report card, the sensible step is usually to keep going and check the next assessment, since school marks tend to lag understanding by a term.

introSummary: IGCSE tutors in South City 1 Gurugram teach Grade 9 and Grade 10 students on Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses, at home in this central pocket, online, or across both. Most families arrive searching for more hours. Marks are usually lost somewhere narrower: answers written to the wrong command term, working left off a maths solution, units dropped in a science calculation. Matching therefore starts with what the student's last paper looked like, not with how many sessions can be squeezed in.

contentBlocks.heading: What South City 1 parents search for, and what actually moves an IGCSE grade in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The search is almost always about quantity. More sessions, longer sessions, an earlier start, someone every day if possible. It is a reasonable instinct and it is usually aimed at the wrong target.

Pull out a student's last IGCSE paper and the losses tend to cluster. A four-mark question answered with one good idea repeated three ways. A maths solution with the right answer and no working, when the method marks were the bulk of the credit. A chemistry calculation correct to the last line and then written without units. A history or business answer that describes when the question said explain. None of that is a knowledge problem, and none of it is fixed by adding a fourth session to the week.

What fixes it is narrow and teachable. The student learns what each command term is asking for, how marks are distributed across an answer, and why examiners reward a because rather than a longer sentence.

The knowledge gaps are real too, of course, and some students genuinely have not understood moles or trigonometry. But those two problems need different treatment, and a tutor who cannot tell them apart after two sessions will treat everything as a content gap. That is the most common reason families here end up paying for a lot of tuition and seeing a small change.

contentBlocks.heading: The two-year IGCSE run as it plays out for South City 1 students in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Grade 9 and Grade 10 form a single course, examined at the end, and the two years do not carry equal weight in how a family should behave. Grade 9 is when subjects are still being chosen or confirmed, when a tier can still be changed without drama, and when a foundation topic can be rebuilt slowly. It is also the year most families skip, because nothing looks urgent yet.

Grade 10 is when the constraints arrive at once. Mocks, coursework deadlines where the school has chosen a coursework route, entry decisions, and a fixed exam series. Cambridge sets June and November series and additionally runs a February and March series in India. Pearson Edexcel runs January alongside May or June. Those dates are set long before a family decides it needs help.

Subject count deserves an honest conversation in Grade 9 rather than a resigned one in Grade 10. Carrying nine subjects when two of them are visibly sinking often produces a weaker overall profile than carrying seven properly.

What comes next matters here too. Students from this pocket commonly go on to the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels, and both assume the Grade 10 understanding was real rather than assembled in the last eight weeks.

Grade 10: mocks, coursework and entries land together
Cambridge June and November, plus February and March in India
Edexcel January and May or June
Seven subjects done well can beat nine done thinly

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 30 to Sector 41: the short-commute advantage around South City 1, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
This pocket sits in the middle of the older city rather than out on one of the newer corridors, and the practical effect on tutoring is favourable. Sector 30, Sector 31, Sector 40 and Sector 41 all lie within a short run, Sushant Lok 1 is next door, and MG Road is close enough that a tutor finishing a session there can be at a South City 1 gate without a serious journey.

That widens the pool of tutors who can realistically hold a weekday evening slot. It also means the two societies alongside, Unitech Heritage City and The Close, share tutors with the main South City 1 blocks rather than competing with them for a scarce few.

South City 2 sits further along and shares a boundary of habit more than of geography, with families in both often using the same names when they compare notes.

The drawback is worth naming. Central location makes this a convenient stop for tutors travelling between two better-paying areas, and a slot squeezed between two others is the first to slip when traffic misbehaves. Ask where the session before yours ends and where the next one starts. A tutor with a clean gap either side will be more reliable than one whose route treats you as a waypoint.
items: Sector 30, 31, 40 and 41 all within a short run
Sushant Lok 1 and MG Road immediately adjacent
Unitech Heritage City and The Close share the same tutor pool
Wider weekday availability than the outer corridors
Avoid being the squeezed middle slot in a tutor's route

contentBlocks.heading: Subject by subject: where South City 1 students lose marks they had already earned
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics is the clearest case. In both Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, a multi-step question awards method marks for a correct approach even when the arithmetic fails at the end. Students who work in their heads and write only the answer forfeit those marks and cannot understand why a correct-looking script scored badly.

The sciences lose marks at the edges rather than the middle. Cambridge Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 all penalise missing units, careless significant figures and answers that state a result without the reasoning step the question asked for. On the practical side, students entered for the alternative to practical paper are being tested on experimental design and error, not on lab dexterity, and that is a distinct thing to revise for.

English, business and the humanities lose marks to structure. A six-mark evaluate question wants a judgement supported both ways, and a student who writes only the supporting side has capped their own score regardless of how well it is written.

Rarer requests come up here as well, including Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and second-language entries. Those tutor pools are thinner, so ask early rather than in the exam term.
items: Method marks in 0580 and 4MA1 need visible working
Units and significant figures decide science edge marks
Alternative to practical tests design and error, not dexterity
Evaluate questions need both sides plus a judgement
Rarer subjects need a longer search runway

contentBlocks.heading: School spread across the South City 1 blocks, Unitech Heritage City and The Close
contentBlocks.body:
Children from these blocks attend a range of international schools rather than one local campus, including Lancers International School, Scottish High International School, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School. Because the pocket is central, bus routes run outward in several directions and no two neighbours are necessarily on the same academic calendar.

The practical consequence for tutoring is about pacing and internal marking. Schools sequence the same syllabus differently, set internal tests of differing severity, and vary in how closely their marking follows published grade descriptors. A student can be doing fine by school marks and still be some way off on a real past paper, or the reverse.

A tutor who has taught students from the same school will already know which of those two situations is likely, and will ask for a past paper rather than trusting the report card.

contentBlocks.heading: Matching an IGCSE tutor to a South City 1 address in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The useful first call is unusually boring. Grade, board, subjects, tier if already decided, school, block or society within South City 1, and the free hours in a normal week. Parents sometimes want to start with the child's character. That comes later, and it is genuinely relevant, but it does not narrow a list.

The most valuable thing a parent can supply is a recent marked paper. One returned school assessment tells an advisor more about the problem than half an hour of description, and it is what allows the shortlist to skew towards a technique-focused tutor or a content-focused one.

Availability is then checked against that specific combination of subject, tier, format and hour. Tutor schedules shift through the year, so what is open in one month may not be in the next, and that is stated openly rather than promised.

You receive a small set of profiles with subject depth, boards and tiers taught, and format offered. The introductory session then works from a real question the student recently got wrong. The tutor should end it able to say which marks were lost to not knowing and which to not showing, and the family should get that in writing.
items: Bring one recent marked paper to the first call
Tier, board, block and free hours collected upfront
Availability checked for that exact combination
Small profile set with tier and format detail
Written split of knowledge gaps versus technique gaps

contentBlocks.heading: Study rooms and screens: choosing a tuition format in South City 1
contentBlocks.body:
Independent houses and larger flats give this pocket an advantage that families rarely think about: most students here have a room with a door, which is the single biggest determinant of whether either format works. A tutor at the dining table with a television running two metres away will lose half the session, and that is true in person as much as online.

Given that, home tutoring works well here. Access is straightforward, parking is manageable in most blocks, and the short internal distances mean a tutor is less likely to arrive frayed. For a Grade 9 student who needs someone watching them attempt a question, that presence is worth paying for.

Online earns its place in two situations. One is subject scarcity, where the person who genuinely knows Computer Science 0478 or an Edexcel Further Pure entry is not going to be driving to Sector 40 on a Tuesday. The other is exam season, when short sessions to clear specific doubts are easier to slot in than visits.

Hybrid tends to win over a full year. In-person teaching at the weekend, a shorter online review midweek where the tutor marks work the student has already done alone.
items: A door that closes matters more than the format
Straightforward home access across most blocks
Home visits suit students who need visible supervision
Online unlocks scarce subjects and exam-week doubts
Hybrid: weekend teaching, midweek marked review

contentBlocks.heading: The extra-hours trap, and what South City 1 families should measure instead
contentBlocks.body:
There is a point past which more tuition makes things worse. A student with four sessions a week has almost no time left to attempt anything alone, and attempting alone is where the learning happens. Sessions where a tutor solves and a student nods feel productive to everyone in the room and produce very little.

Three things are worth measuring instead. How many full questions did the student attempt unaided this week. How many of those were marked against the official scheme rather than checked for the final answer. And can the tutor name, today, which topics are secure and which are not.

On fees, the drivers are scarcity, level and travel. Exam-year work is priced above Grade 9 work, uncommon subjects above common ones, and a home visit above the same tutor's online rate because of the journey. Rates should be clear before any introductory session.

The limitation to state plainly: no tutor can produce a grade, and anyone offering one should be treated with suspicion. What good tutoring produces is a student who knows what the question is asking and has practised answering it. The grade follows from that, or occasionally it does not, and honest tutors say so.
items: Past a point, more sessions crowd out independent practice
Count unaided attempts, not hours attended
Insist work is marked to the official scheme
Fees move with scarcity, level and travel
No tutor can promise a grade

contentBlocks.heading: The checks that stand between a tutor profile and your home
contentBlocks.body:
Screening is designed to test specificity, because vague experience claims are the easiest thing in the world to make. Identity is confirmed against a government-issued document before any home visit is discussed. Qualifications are checked against the subject being offered, not against teaching in the abstract.

The subject conversation goes into detail. Which syllabus codes have been taught and over how many cohorts. Which tier. In the sciences, whether students sat the practical test or the alternative to practical paper. In maths, how the tutor teaches a student to lay out working so method marks survive an arithmetic slip. Answers that stay general are a signal in themselves.

A working interaction follows, on a question at the level a family has actually asked about, because teaching a struggling Grade 10 student is not the same skill as knowing the material.

Deliberately outside the scope: outcomes. No tutor is verified as having produced particular results, no ratings are invented, and no testimonials are attributed to families who did not give them. Where a tutor is new to the platform and has limited references, that is stated rather than smoothed over. Home visits remain subject to tutor availability and confirmed timings.
items: Government ID verified before home visits are arranged
Qualifications matched to the specific subject offered
Syllabus codes, tiers and practical routes probed
Live teaching interaction at the requested level
No invented ratings, results or testimonials

faqs.question: Every listing says best IGCSE tutor. How do we separate a good one from a confident one?
faqs.answer: Ask three specific questions on the first call. Which syllabus code do you teach and at which tier. What does a four-mark explain question need that a four-mark describe question does not. And how would you spend the first session with a student who scored badly on a paper you have not seen. A strong tutor answers all three concretely and briefly. Someone who talks about personalised methods and student potential without touching the actual papers is telling you they do not work at that level of detail.

faqs.question: What is the real difference between describe and explain in an IGCSE answer?
faqs.answer: Describe asks what happens. Explain asks why it happens, and the marks depend on a causal link being stated. A student who writes the plants grew taller in the light has described. A student who writes the plants grew taller because more light allowed a higher rate of photosynthesis has explained, and picks up the mark the first answer missed. Other command terms carry their own expectations: suggest applies known ideas to an unfamiliar situation, compare needs both things in the same sentence, and evaluate needs a judgement, not just two lists.

faqs.question: Is small-group tuition in South City 1 worth considering instead of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It can work when the students are on the same board, the same tier and roughly the same point in the syllabus, and when the difficulty is shared rather than individual. Those conditions are less common than they sound, particularly in a pocket where neighbours attend different schools with different pacing. One-to-one is the safer choice for a student with a specific gap, since group time gets spent on whichever student asks most. If cost is the driver, a shorter one-to-one session usually beats a longer group one.

faqs.question: How much past paper practice is actually useful?
faqs.answer: Less than most families assume, if it is done without mark schemes. Working through twenty papers and checking only final answers teaches almost nothing, because the marks live in the steps. A better pattern is fewer papers, each one attempted under timed conditions, then marked against that paper's own official scheme, with the examiner report read for the questions that went badly. Two papers treated that way generally teach more than ten skimmed. Past papers also work poorly before the syllabus is covered, so timing matters as much as volume.

faqs.question: My child understands everything during the session but blanks in the test. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually recognition being mistaken for recall. Following an explanation feels like understanding, and it is a much weaker state than being able to start a question from a blank page. The fix is uncomfortable and simple: the student attempts problems alone, under time, before the tutor explains anything, and the session works on what failed. Expect resistance for a few weeks. Any tutor whose sessions consist mostly of the tutor writing on paper while the student watches is reinforcing exactly the habit that produces this.

faqs.question: We live in an independent house here. Does that make home tutoring the better option?
faqs.answer: It helps, mainly because of the study room. A session behind a closed door with no television and no younger sibling in the room is worth more than any format decision. Access and parking are also easier across most of these blocks than in the high-rise corridors, so tutors arrive on time more often. The one thing a house does not fix is subject scarcity, and if the subject you need is uncommon, an online specialist will beat a nearby generalist regardless of how good the study room is.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need to have been an examiner?
faqs.answer: It is a useful signal, not a requirement, and it is frequently claimed loosely. What actually matters is whether the tutor works from official mark schemes and examiner reports and can show you where marks are awarded in a specific answer. A tutor who has never marked officially but marks every piece of homework against the published scheme is more useful than one with a marking history who does not do that with your child. Ask to see a marked piece of the student's work after two or three sessions.

faqs.question: Should we start all three sciences together or fix one first?
faqs.answer: Fix one first in most cases. Three simultaneous science tutors consume the evenings entirely and leave no room for the independent practice that makes any of it stick. Choose the subject where the gap is widest or where the foundation topic blocks the most later material, chemistry moles being the classic example. Once that subject is running steadily and the student is attempting work unaided, add the second. Families who start everything at once in Grade 10 usually end up dropping two of the three by mid-year anyway.

faqs.question: How far ahead of Grade 10 exams should revision-focused tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Roughly one to two terms ahead, and it depends on whether the syllabus is finished. Revision on material the school has not yet taught is not revision, it is teaching ahead, which is a different and slower exercise. A workable sequence is content support through Grade 9 and the first part of Grade 10, a shift to timed past papers with proper marking once each topic is covered, and a final stretch focused on the specific question types that keep going wrong. Starting revision-only work six weeks out limits what can change.

heroTitle: IGCSE Tutors in South City 2, Gurugram
heroSubtitle: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel support for Grade 9 and Grade 10 students living around South City 2, Nirvana Country, Unitech Fresco and Orchid Petals. Sessions can run at home off Sohna Road, online across Gurugram, or split across the week. Shortlists are built around paper entry, tier and the slots your family can actually keep.
introSummary: IGCSE tutors in South City 2 Gurugram usually work with Grade 9 and Grade 10 students following Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, either at home near Sohna Road and the Sector 47 to 50 belt, or online. What separates a useful tutor from an expensive one is timing. Grade 9 tutoring builds the content base. Grade 10 tutoring is mostly exam technique against fixed paper entries. After the December mocks, the honest scope narrows to two or three subjects rather than the whole set.

contentBlocks.heading: Where a South City 2, Gurugram Family Stands in the IGCSE Year
contentBlocks.body:
Families here tend to arrive on this page in one of three months. September, when Grade 10 has just started and the first unit tests came back worse than expected. January, once the mock results are out. Or March, which is late, though not pointless.

The IGCSE year has a fixed shape and it helps to know it before paying anyone. Grade 9 lays down syllabus content and almost none of it is externally examined, which is exactly why it gets neglected. Grade 10 is the year of entries: schools normally lock subject codes, tier and paper combinations several months ahead of a May or June series, and around the turn of the year for a November series. Where a school runs coursework instead of an alternative paper, drafting and internal moderation happen well before the exam window opens.

So the practical reading on timing. Starting in Grade 9 buys understanding. Starting in early Grade 10 buys technique. Starting after mocks buys triage on two or three papers, not on eight subjects at once.

Most enquiries from South City 2 are the third kind. The work is still worth doing. It is simply narrower than parents expect.
items: Grade 9: content gaps, lab skills, writing habits
Early Grade 10: past papers against the actual entry
Post-mock: two or three subjects, triage only
Entry codes and tier decided by the school, not the tutor
November series planning starts around the turn of the year

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 47 to Sector 50: The Streets Either Side of South City 2
contentBlocks.body:
South City 2 sits with Sohna Road on one shoulder and the central sectors on the other. Sector 47, Sector 49 and Sector 50 are the immediate neighbours, and a tutor who already teaches inside one of them is rarely more than a short run away from your gate. South City 1 is close enough that the same tutor often covers both. Nirvana Country, Unitech Fresco and Orchid Petals come up constantly in enquiries from this pocket, and each has its own gate procedure that eats five to ten minutes off a session if nobody warns the tutor in advance.

That detail matters more than it sounds. A 6:30 pm slot that becomes a 6:45 pm start twice a week costs you roughly an hour a month.

Travel in this pocket is easier east and west than it is north. Reaching Golf Course Road in the evening peak is unpredictable, so a tutor based on that side may quote a later slot or ask for a weekend block instead. Tutors coming up Sohna Road from the Vatika Chowk direction usually have the smoother run. Availability across any of these addresses depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed when you enquire.

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Split Weeks for IGCSE Students in South City 2, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Three arrangements are common in this part of Gurugram, and they suit different problems.

Home tutoring works when the student needs a person physically present to stop the drift: a Grade 9 child who quietly does nothing for forty minutes on a video call, or a student working through Chemistry practical write-ups where equipment, glassware sketches and messy tables are easier to correct over a shoulder. An IGCSE home tutor in South City 2 is most realistic in the 5 pm to 8 pm band on weekdays.

Online suits the opposite case. Rarer combinations, Additional Maths alongside the main syllabus, Economics at Extended tier, or a specific Edexcel paper, have a much wider pool of teachers once you stop insisting they drive to Sohna Road. Screen-shared past papers with a document camera on the student's side work well for marking.

A split week is what many families settle on. One home session for the subject that needs supervision, one online session for the subject that needs a specialist.

The honest limitation: online is worse for a student who has already stopped trying. Attention has to be borrowed from somewhere, and a screen does not lend it.

Online: rare subject and paper combinations, later slots
Hybrid: one supervised session, one specialist session
Weekday home slots cluster between 5 pm and 8 pm
Online is the weaker option for a disengaged student

contentBlocks.heading: 0580, 0620 and 0625: The Codes Sitting Behind the Subject Names
contentBlocks.body:
Parents ask for a maths tutor. Examiners mark a specific paper. The gap between those two sentences is where a lot of tuition money goes to waste.

Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, and the Extended route runs Paper 2 and Paper 4 with a materially harder question style. Additional Mathematics 0606 is a separate qualification, taken alongside 0580 by stronger students, and it introduces calculus and further trigonometry that a general maths tutor may not have taught in years. Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 both end with either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and only the school knows which one your child is entered for. Biology 0610, Economics 0455 and First Language English 0500 each turn on command-term discipline more than on content recall.

Pearson Edexcel runs its own codes. International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1 uses Papers 1 and 2 at Foundation or Higher tier, and the tier decision caps the top grade available.

Before the first session, find the code and the tier on your child's school portal or report. An IGCSE maths tutor for South City 2 who is told 0580 Extended plus 0606 will plan a different term to one who is simply told Grade 10 maths.

Additional Maths 0606 is a separate qualification
0620 and 0625: practical test or alternative-to-practical
Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation tier caps the achievable grade
0500 and 0455 reward command-term precision over recall

contentBlocks.heading: From First Message to a Named Tutor Near South City 2, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
The sequence is short and deliberately unglamorous.

One: you send the subject, the board, the grade and, if you have it, the paper entry. Two: an advisor calls to establish the actual problem, which is often narrower than the enquiry suggested. A student described as weak at physics frequently turns out to be fine at mechanics and lost in electricity. Three: a shortlist is put together from tutors who have taught that board at that level and who have a slot that fits your evenings. Four: a first session, treated as a diagnostic rather than a lesson. Five: a short written plan for the coming weeks, and only then a regular schedule.

What the first session should produce is a list. Topics secure, topics shaky, topics untouched, plus one habit to change immediately. If you finish an hour and have only heard that your child is bright and needs confidence, ask for something more specific or ask for a different tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 Is Groundwork, Grade 10 Is the Exam Year
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE runs across two school years, and they ask for completely different things.

In Grade 9 the syllabus is being introduced. Nothing external is riding on it, which is exactly why marks slip without anyone worrying. A tutor's job in this year is unfashionable: algebraic fluency, unit handling, structured lab reports, reading a question twice before writing. Get this year right and Grade 10 becomes a revision problem rather than a rescue.

Grade 10 is different work. The syllabus finishes somewhere in the second or third term, entries are already fixed, and everything after that is past papers, mark scheme literacy and time discipline. A student who understands the physics but writes three lines where the mark scheme wants a formula, a substitution and a unit will keep losing the same two marks all year.

Support runs across the Grade 1 to Grade 12 range, and the pre-IGCSE years around Grade 7 and 8 are often where the arithmetic and writing habits that later cost marks are set.

One caution for South City 2 parents. Bringing in a tutor in Grade 10 for a subject never understood in Grade 9 means re-teaching two years inside one. It can be done. It is not comfortable.

Grade 10: past papers, mark schemes, timing under pressure

faqs.question: My son is in Grade 10 and mocks are already over. Is it too late to bring in a tutor?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the scope changes. With mocks behind you and entries already fixed, the sensible plan is two or three subjects rather than the full set, chosen from where the mock paper shows recoverable marks. Recoverable usually means method errors, missing units, unread questions and untouched final parts, not whole topics never understood. Ask the tutor to mark the actual mock script in the first session and to name the marks that were available and lost. If the answer is that most losses are conceptual across every topic, be realistic about what eight weeks can do.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is entered for the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: The school decides this, usually at the point of entry, and it appears on the entry confirmation or the subject information the school shares with parents. The class teacher will tell you if you ask directly. It matters because the two papers reward different preparation. A practical test needs apparatus handling, observation and recording under supervision. The alternative paper needs the ability to read a described experiment, spot the control variable, criticise a method and complete a results table on paper. Tell the tutor which one applies before the first session, otherwise half the preparation goes to the wrong skill.

faqs.question: We live inside Unitech Fresco. Will a tutor actually come into the society for an evening session?
faqs.answer: Home sessions around Unitech Fresco, Orchid Petals and Nirvana Country are arranged regularly, though it depends on which tutor has a free slot and where they are travelling from. Two things help. Give the society name and tower at the enquiry stage rather than a general area, and clear visitor entry in advance so the tutor is not waiting at the gate. Evening slots between 5 pm and 8 pm fill first. If your preferred subject has few local teachers, an online slot may be offered instead, which is a genuine trade rather than a downgrade.

faqs.question: Is Additional Maths 0606 worth taking, or will it just pull down the main maths grade?
faqs.answer: It depends on where the student sits in Extended 0580. A student comfortably handling Paper 4 algebra and trigonometry usually gains from 0606, because the calculus and further functions work makes the main syllabus feel routine and it gives a head start on AS or IB Higher Level maths later. A student still fighting Paper 2 basics will find 0606 takes time away from the grade that matters more. Ask the school what proportion of the cohort takes it and whether it is taught in class hours or expected largely from home.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition near South City 2 usually cost, and does online work out cheaper?
faqs.answer: Fees are quoted per session and depend on subject, level and mode rather than on a single rate card. Online is commonly quoted lower for the same tutor because no travel time is being paid for. Rare combinations cost more, since fewer teachers can take them. Sciences at Extended tier and Additional Maths typically sit above general Grade 9 support. You will see the fee alongside a specific tutor profile and a proposed schedule before committing to anything, and there is no requirement to book a long block up front.

faqs.question: The school teaches Cambridge but my daughter's cousin follows Edexcel. Can one tutor handle both?
faqs.answer: Some can, many should not be asked to. The content overlap between Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 is large, but the paper structure, mark scheme wording and tier rules differ enough that a tutor who has only ever taught one board will guess at the other. For a single student it is far better to match to the board the school has entered them for. If two children in one family follow different boards, it is usually cleaner to run two tutors than to stretch one across both syllabuses.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do Grade 10 students around Sohna Road normally take?
faqs.answer: Two sessions a week for one subject is the common pattern, and three subjects at two sessions each is close to the ceiling before school work starts suffering. Families sometimes want daily sessions after a bad mock. That usually backfires, because past-paper practice needs gaps in which the student attempts questions alone. A reasonable rhythm is one teaching session, independent work, then one review session where the attempted work is marked. If a student is genuinely behind in five subjects, the conversation should be about priorities, not about adding hours.

faqs.question: Does my child need to keep going to school tuition and this at the same time?
faqs.answer: Often no, and stacking both is one of the more expensive mistakes families make. School remedial classes, a coaching centre batch and a private tutor can end up covering the same chapter three times while the actual weakness stays untouched. Pick the one that gives individual diagnosis. A group batch is reasonable for content coverage and poor at spotting why one particular student keeps losing method marks. If you keep both, make sure they are doing different jobs and tell the tutor what the batch is covering each week.

faqs.question: We may move to Delhi or Noida during Grade 10. Does that end the tutoring arrangement?
faqs.answer: It does not have to. A home arrangement clearly ends when you leave the area, but the same tutor can often continue online, which is one reason some families run at least one subject online from the start. IGCSE itself travels well, since the qualification is the same wherever the school sits, though a new school may enter students for different papers or a different tier. Tell the advisor about a likely move at the enquiry stage so the plan does not depend entirely on someone driving to South City 2.

introSummary: IGCSE tutors in Sushant Lok 1 Gurugram exist to do the part of the job a classroom cannot. A subject teacher carries twenty-eight students through a fixed syllabus on a fixed calendar and marks to a common standard. A tutor works with one student, which means they can stop on the single topic that broke three months ago, watch how a question is attempted rather than only what was written, and rebuild method before content. contentBlocks.heading: What a Class Teacher Cannot Do for a Sushant Lok 1 Student in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
A good school teacher and a good tutor are not doing the same work, and confusing the two is the fastest way to waste a term.

The teacher owns coverage. They have a syllabus to finish by a date, a class of twenty-five or thirty moving at an average pace, internal assessment to set and moderate, and a professional obligation to treat every student the same way. They cannot spend forty minutes on the one student who never really understood mole calculations, because twenty-seven others already did.

The tutor owns diagnosis. One student, one hour, no class average. That allows things a classroom cannot afford: watching a question being attempted live instead of reading the finished answer, tracing an error back two chapters, asking the student to explain a definition aloud and hearing exactly where the wording goes soft.

Parents around Sushant Lok 1 often ask for a tutor to re-teach the day's lesson. That is the least valuable version of the arrangement. The useful version starts one level below the lesson, finds what is missing, and fixes it while school carries on above.

The first session is a diagnostic. Expect the tutor to work through recent school assessments or a past-paper section and come back with a short written breakdown: what is secure, what is shaky, what has never been covered, and one working habit to change this week. If nothing written arrives within a few days, that is worth raising immediately rather than at the end of the month.

contentBlocks.heading: Two Years, Two Jobs: Grade 9 Diagnosis and Grade 10 Rehearsal
contentBlocks.body:
The same student needs different tutoring in each of the two IGCSE years, and the switch catches families out.

Grade 9 is diagnostic work. Nothing external is being marked, the school is introducing new content quickly, and weak foundations hide easily behind classroom marks that still look acceptable. This is the year to fix algebraic manipulation, scientific notation, essay paragraphing and the discipline of reading a full question. Unfashionable, slow, and worth more than anything done later.

Grade 10 is rehearsal. The content is largely known, entries are fixed, and the remaining marks sit in technique. Knowing the difference between describe, explain, compare and evaluate. Recognising a six-mark question and budgeting time for it. Writing the formula, the substitution and the unit rather than a bare number.

Students younger than this are supported too, across the Grade 1 to Grade 12 range, and the years just before IGCSE are often where the habits that later cost marks get set.

The uncomfortable version. A student starting tuition in the second term of Grade 10 with two years of gaps is being asked to do diagnosis and rehearsal at once, on a shrinking calendar. Possible. Rarely pleasant.

contentBlocks.heading: Biology, Business Studies and the Papers That Punish Vague Answers
contentBlocks.body:
Some IGCSE subjects fail students on knowledge. Others fail them on precision, and those are the ones where one-to-one work pays quickly.

Cambridge Biology 0610 is the classic example. Students know the process and still lose marks because the answer says the cell gets bigger rather than naming osmosis, water potential and the direction of movement. Business Studies 0450 does the same with case-study questions, where an answer that describes when the mark scheme wants justification scores half. Economics 0455 rewards a diagram drawn correctly and labelled fully, and quietly penalises a paragraph that says the same thing in words.

English splits two ways. First Language English 0500 assumes native-level control and marks writing craft. English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511 are different qualifications with different papers, and a school choosing one over the other has made a judgement about the student.

Computer Science 0478 catches families out because the theory paper carries more weight than the practical work most students enjoy.

Pearson Edexcel runs parallel codes such as 4BI1 for Biology. Bring the code and the tier to the first call so an IGCSE science tutor for Sushant Lok 1 plans against the right paper.

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, Fit and the Month That Tells You Whether It Is Working
contentBlocks.body:
Fees are per session and move with level, subject scarcity and travel. Higher-tier sciences and less commonly taught subjects sit above general support, because fewer teachers can take them. The same tutor is usually quoted lower online, since no travel is being paid for. You see the number against a named profile and a proposed schedule before agreeing to anything.

Fit is separate from competence and matters just as much. A tutor may be excellent and still wrong for a particular child, and saying so after two or three sessions is normal. A replacement shortlist follows without argument.

Four weeks is the honest review point. By then you should be able to see marked work with lost marks annotated, a topic list where items have moved from shaky to secure, and a student who can explain something aloud they could not explain a month earlier. Improved report card grades take longer than that, and anyone promising them on a timeline is guessing.

The limits are worth stating. Tuition does not compensate for skipped school homework, does not fix a subject the student has privately given up on, and cannot rebuild two years in eight weeks.

Identity documents are verified. Claimed qualifications are checked. Where a tutor has worked with families previously, references are sought.

What none of that establishes is the thing you actually care about. Whether your child will admit confusion in front of this person. Whether the pace suits. Whether week three still feels productive. Documents cannot show any of it, which is why the first session is treated as a trial and why an early change is expected rather than resented.

For home sessions in Sushant Lok 1, tutors are expected to hold to agreed timings, teach in a shared area of the home, and give notice of any change rather than sending a message at six for a seven o'clock slot.

faqs.question: My daughter's school teacher is good. Why would we add a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Because the two jobs differ. A strong class teacher covers the syllabus properly, moderates internal work and keeps thirty students moving together. What they cannot do is stop for forty minutes on one student's specific misunderstanding, or watch how that student attempts a question rather than reading the finished answer. If your daughter is broadly following the class and losing marks on precision, a tutor working one-to-one can find the pattern quickly. If she is lost on whole topics, the tutor is filling a gap the classroom pace created rather than duplicating anything.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor realistic inside Sushant Lok 1, or does everything end up online?
faqs.answer: Home sessions are arranged here regularly, helped by the central position between Sector 43, South City 1 and DLF Phase 4. A tutor already teaching nearby can often add a slot without much extra travel. Two practical points. Evening slots between five and eight fill fastest, so flexibility on the day widens your options considerably. And parking near the older blocks is awkward, so mention where the tutor should leave a car when you book. If your subject has few local teachers, an online slot may be the stronger match.

faqs.question: What is the actual difference between First Language English 0500 and English as a Second Language 0510?
faqs.answer: They are separate qualifications with different papers and different expectations. First Language English assumes the student handles English at native level and marks writing craft, structure, tone and reading response at a demanding standard. English as a Second Language tests comprehension, controlled writing and language accuracy, and is graded on that basis. Schools decide which one a student is entered for, and the decision is made on the student's demonstrated command of the language. Ask which one applies before booking, because preparing for the wrong paper wastes an entire term of sessions.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my son is losing marks on content or on how he writes answers?
faqs.answer: Look at a marked script rather than a percentage. If the working is right and the final answer is right but marks are still missing, the problem is presentation: no unit, no formula shown, no substitution line. If he writes fluently but never answers the command term the question asked, that is technique. If the page is blank or the method starts wrongly, that is content. Most Grade 10 students are a mix. A tutor should be able to separate the three in the first session and tell you which is costing the most.

faqs.question: How are fees decided for IGCSE tuition near Sushant Lok 1, and can we start with one subject?
faqs.answer: Fees are quoted per session and depend on the level, how scarce the subject is and whether the tutor travels. Higher-tier sciences and less commonly taught subjects sit above general support because the pool of qualified teachers is smaller. Online is usually quoted below a home visit with the same person. Starting with one subject is the sensible route and the one most families take. It lets you judge the arrangement on evidence before extending it, and adding a second subject later is straightforward if the first is going well.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor teach Physics and Chemistry to a Grade 10 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Some tutors are genuinely strong across both, particularly at Core level. At Extended tier the two diverge, and a chemistry specialist asked to cover electricity and moments often teaches it competently rather than well. A reasonable test is to ask each candidate which of the two they would rather not teach. The honest ones answer. If the student is weak in both, two tutors usually produce better results than one, even though it costs more to run.

faqs.question: My child gets nervous with new people. How is that handled in the first session?
faqs.answer: Tell the advisor before the shortlist is built, because it changes who gets suggested. Some tutors are patient with a quiet start and spend the first twenty minutes on low-pressure work; others move fast and suit a confident student. For a nervous child, a home session is often easier than a screen, since familiar surroundings help. Keep the first session short if that helps. And accept that one session is not enough evidence either way. Judge by week three, when a child who is going to open up usually has.

faqs.question: Should we also enrol in a coaching batch near Sushant Lok 1 at the same time?
faqs.answer: Usually not for the same subject. A batch and a one-to-one tutor covering the same chapter means paying twice for coverage while the individual weakness stays unaddressed, and it eats the evenings the student needs for independent practice. Group coaching does content delivery reasonably and diagnosis poorly. If you keep both, give them separate jobs, tell the tutor what the batch is covering each week, and watch the total hours. A Grade 10 student with school, a batch, a tutor and activities has no time left to actually practise.

faqs.question: What if my son does not improve after two months of sessions?
faqs.answer: Ask for the evidence first, then decide. Marked past-paper work, a topic list showing what has moved, and the tutor's own account of what is still blocking progress. Three explanations are common: the sessions are being used to re-teach class content rather than fix the underlying gap, the student is not attempting anything between sessions, or the fit is wrong. Each has a different remedy. Changing tutors solves only the third. If nothing has been written down in two months, that alone tells you the arrangement was not being run properly.

A tutor coming from Sector 56 is four kilometres away and can be at your gate in ten minutes at noon. contentBlocks.heading: The Two Years That Decide an IGCSE Grade
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is a two-year course and the years reward completely different effort.

Year one, Grade 9, is where content is laid down and where almost nothing external is at stake. That safety is deceptive. A student can coast through internal tests on short-term memory and reach Grade 10 without secure algebra, without a reliable way of structuring an extended answer, and without ever having read a full question properly. Tutoring in this year is quiet, unspectacular repair work.

Year two is examination craft. Content is finishing, entries are locked, and marks now hinge on how answers are built. Where the mark scheme wants a formula, a substitution and a unit, three separate marks are on offer and a bare correct number collects one.

Schools also decide the tier. Core caps the grade band available, Extended opens the top of it, and moving between them late in the course is not always possible. Ask which tier your child is on and why.

Support is available across the Grade 1 to Grade 12 range, and the two years before IGCSE begins are often the cheapest place to fix what later becomes expensive.

References are requested where a tutor has worked with families before, and punctuality and communication are the two things previous families are asked about most.

What cannot be confirmed in advance is whether this person will work for your child. Confidence in front of a stranger, tolerance for being corrected, whether the pace lands. Documents say nothing about any of it.

That is why the first session is treated as a trial, why an early switch is unremarkable, and why no long commitment is asked for at the start. For home visits in Sushant Lok 2, tutors are expected to keep to agreed timings and to teach in a shared area of the flat.

faqs.question: What is the earliest realistic weekday slot for a tutor coming to a tower in Sushant Lok 2?
faqs.answer: For most Grade 10 students here, six in the evening is the earliest that works properly, and half past six is safer. The limiting factor is rarely the tutor. It is the school bus, which on longer routes drops students after five, followed by food and a short break before anything useful can happen. Add visitor registration at the gate and a shared lift and a nominal five-thirty start often becomes five-fifty. If your child is home by four, an earlier slot is genuinely possible and worth asking about.

faqs.question: My son takes Coordinated Sciences rather than separate Physics and Chemistry. Does that change who we need?
faqs.answer: It changes the brief considerably. Coordinated and Combined Sciences cover all three disciplines within a smaller number of papers, so the depth in each is different from the single-subject syllabuses and the paper structure is its own thing. A tutor who only teaches separate Physics will over-teach some topics and miss the balance the paper actually wants. Ask candidates directly whether they have taught the combined route and how many cohorts through it. Also check what your son intends to study after Grade 10, since the route can affect readiness for A Level sciences.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a compromise, or is it genuinely equal for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: For a motivated Grade 10 student it is close to equal, and in some situations it is better. Past papers screen-share cleanly, the tutor can annotate a scanned answer in real time, and removing travel means access to teachers who have taught the specific paper your school entered your child for. Where it falls behind is supervision. A younger or disengaged student drifts faster on a call, and any work needing the tutor to see a full page of untidy working is slower. Judge by the student, not by the format.

faqs.question: How many marks does answer technique actually cost, compared with not knowing the content?
faqs.answer: More than most parents expect. On a typical Grade 10 science script, a meaningful share of lost marks come from answers that are correct in substance but incomplete in form: no unit, no working shown, a description offered where the command term asked for an explanation, or a final question left blank because time ran out. None of that requires new content teaching. It requires drilling against mark schemes. This is also why marks can move noticeably in a few weeks in one subject while barely shifting in another where the content itself is missing.

faqs.question: We live in a tower with strict visitor rules. Does that complicate a home tutor arrangement?
faqs.answer: It adds a step rather than a problem, provided you handle it in advance. Register the tutor as a recurring visitor if your society allows it, rather than approving an app request every week while the tutor waits at the boundary. Share the tower number and floor at the point of booking, not on the day. Where a society restricts entry for regular service visits, say so at the enquiry stage so an online arrangement is proposed from the start instead of a home slot that later has to be unwound.

faqs.question: How are fees set for IGCSE tuition near Sushant Lok 2, and is there a joining commitment?
faqs.answer: Fees are quoted per session against a specific tutor and depend on the level, how scarce the subject is and whether travel is involved. Extended-tier sciences and less commonly taught subjects sit above general support because fewer teachers can take them. Online with the same person is normally lower than a home visit. No block booking is required to begin, and you see the figure alongside the profile and the proposed schedule before agreeing to anything. Most families start with a single subject and add a second only if the first is working.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my daughter decide whether to take Extended or stay on Core?
faqs.answer: A tutor can give a view, but the school makes the entry decision and knows the internal evidence. What a tutor adds is an independent read after a few weeks: whether the harder paper is within reach with focused work, or whether pushing for it risks a weaker overall result. The consequence matters, because Core caps the grade band available while Extended opens the top of it. Raise it early. Once entries are submitted, changing tier is often not straightforward, and a late switch leaves very little preparation time.

faqs.question: My child says tuition is pointless and does not want a tutor. Should we still arrange one?
faqs.answer: Say so honestly at the enquiry stage, because it changes which tutor suits. A reluctant student needs someone who begins by rebuilding a small amount of confidence rather than opening a past paper in the first ten minutes, and a home session usually works better than a screen for that. Set a short trial period out loud, three or four sessions, and let your child know it is being reviewed. Forcing a long commitment on an unwilling teenager tends to produce attendance without learning, which costs the same and achieves less.

faqs.question: Can sessions pause during school mock weeks and family travel?
faqs.answer: Yes, and telling the tutor in advance matters more than the pause itself. Mock weeks are usually the wrong time to add teaching hours, since the student needs revision time and sleep rather than another new topic. A short break is often sensible. What causes problems is an unannounced gap of several weeks, after which the tutor has no idea what was covered in class meanwhile. Give notice, agree what the student will attempt independently, and book the restart date before the break rather than after it.

heroTitle: IGCSE Tutors in Sushant Lok 3
heroSubtitle: Sushant Lok 3 sits on the Sector 57 side of Golf Course Extension Road, close to Ireo Skyon, M3M Merlin and Emaar DigiHomes. This page sets out what to settle before you book IGCSE tuition here: board, tier, papers, travel time, and whether home or online suits your week.
introSummary: Most searches for IGCSE tutors in Sushant Lok 3 Gurugram start with a booking question, but the useful questions come first. Which board is your child sitting, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel? Core or Extended tier? Which papers, and which series, May or November? A tutor who cannot answer those three things about your child's course will teach content that looks correct and still misses marks. IB Gram matches on that detail first, then on location and timing around Sector 57.

contentBlocks.heading: What a Sushant Lok 3 parent should settle before booking an IGCSE tutor
contentBlocks.body:
Start with the syllabus code printed on your child's timetable. Cambridge IGCSE subjects carry four-digit codes, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE codes are written differently again. That code tells a tutor which content list and which paper pattern apply, and it removes a whole category of wasted sessions. If it is not on the report card, the school office will have it.

Second, the tier. Cambridge offers several subjects in a Core and an Extended version, and the tier decides both the papers sat and the grade band a candidate can reach. A student moved from Extended down to Core in October is now on a different course from the one they began in April. Tuition has to follow that decision rather than quietly argue with it.

Third, name what is actually going wrong. Parents here usually open with a falling grade. Tutors need the layer underneath. Is the content not learnt, learnt but not retrievable under exam time pressure, or written out correctly in substance and marked down in form because the command term said explain and the child described?

Those three answers reshape a shortlist far more than anything else on this page. Only after them does the practical layer matter: whether a tutor can reach Sector 57 by seven in the evening, and whether the week has room for two sessions or one.
items: Syllabus code from the timetable, not just the subject name
Core or Extended, and when the tier was last reviewed
The series the child is entered for
Content gap, recall gap or command-term gap
Realistic evening slots after school and travel

contentBlocks.heading: Home, online or hybrid IGCSE tuition in Sushant Lok 3, Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Home tuition in Sushant Lok 3 is workable, and it is also the option that narrows your choices most. A tutor coming to Ireo Skyon, M3M Merlin or Emaar DigiHomes has to cross Golf Course Extension Road at the same hour every other commuter does. Gate registration in the high-rises adds another few minutes at each end. So a tutor who is excellent on Chemistry Paper 4 but lives towards Dwarka Expressway will simply not take a 6:30pm slot here, and pretending otherwise wastes a fortnight.

Online sessions remove that constraint entirely. For subjects where the specialist pool is thin, such as Additional Mathematics or Economics, online is often the only way to reach someone who has taught the paper repeatedly rather than someone available nearby.

Hybrid is the arrangement most Sushant Lok 3 families settle into after the first month. One in-person session a week, usually at a weekend, for the slow diagnostic work: marking a past paper together, watching how the child sets out a calculation, correcting handwriting habits that cost method marks. The second session runs online midweek, shorter, for doubt-solving on whatever the school covered.

Availability in any of these formats depends on tutor schedules and can be reviewed when you share the subject and the timing you need.
items: Gate and visitor registration inside the towers adds real minutes
Golf Course Extension Road at 6pm to 8pm is the binding constraint
Rare subjects match better online than within a 3km radius
Weekend in-person plus midweek online is the common settlement
Slots subject to tutor availability, not guaranteed on request

contentBlocks.heading: Which IGCSE subjects families near Sector 57 ask about most
contentBlocks.body:
Mathematics leads, and it splits two ways. Extended Mathematics is the usual request, while Additional Mathematics is the one that catches families out, because it moves into calculus and functions at a pace most students meet for the first time in Grade 10. A tutor who has only taught the main Mathematics syllabus will struggle with it.

The sciences come next, and here parents around Sector 57 often ask for one tutor to hold Physics, Chemistry and Biology together. That works at Core level. At Extended it usually does not, because the three papers reward different writing habits, and depth in one rarely travels to the others.

English requests divide by which English the school entered the child for: First Language English and English as a Second Language are separate syllabuses with separate demands, and the wrong assumption about which one a child sits is surprisingly common.

Then there are the humanities and commerce subjects, Economics and Business Studies especially, where marks turn on structured written answers rather than on knowing more facts. Global Perspectives, where offered, needs a tutor comfortable with research write-ups.

We do not claim coverage of every subject at every level in every timeslot. Some combinations take longer to match than others, and a few will not match at all in the window you want.
items: Extended Mathematics, plus Additional Mathematics as a separate skill
Physics, Chemistry and Biology usually need separate specialists at Extended
First Language English and ESL are different syllabuses
Economics and Business Studies reward answer structure over recall
Rare subject and timeslot pairings may not be matchable

contentBlocks.heading: Where Sushant Lok 3 sits, and what that does to travel time in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Sushant Lok 3 is on the Sector 57 side, tucked against Golf Course Extension Road rather than the older Golf Course Road. That single distinction changes the tutor pool. Sushant Lok 2 is close enough that a tutor covering one will usually cover the other. Sector 56 and Sector 62 sit within a reasonable evening run. The Sector Road and HUDA sectors cluster feeds in from the other side.

Go further and it gets harder honestly. Nirvana Country, South City 1 and Sector 65 are all named as nearby on paper, and in a 7pm crawl they are not close at all. A tutor living in DLF Phase 1 or Phase 4 can reach Sushant Lok 3 on a Sunday morning and will think twice about a Wednesday evening.

The useful way to use this is to widen the map by mode rather than by distance. Keep home sessions to the Sector 56 to Sector 62 band, where a tutor can commit without resenting the trip, and put anything beyond that band online.

Families who ignore the band tend to lose tutors after six or seven weeks, not because the teaching failed but because the commute did.

Golf Course Extension Road, not the older Golf Course Road corridor
Sector Road and the HUDA sectors cluster on the inner side
Nirvana Country, South City 1 and Sector 65 read close and travel far

contentBlocks.heading: Grade 9 to Grade 11: the IGCSE timeline behind a Sushant Lok 3 booking
contentBlocks.body:
IGCSE is normally taught across two years, Grade 9 and Grade 10, with the examined series at the end. Schools around Sector 57 differ on how much Grade 9 counts. Some finish nearly half the syllabus in the first year and revisit it lightly. Others treat Grade 9 as a foundation year and compress the examined content into Grade 10, which is when parents suddenly find their child is three chapters behind in two subjects at once.

The main sittings are the May series and the November series. Some centres in India also enter candidates for an earlier series in the year, and whether your school does is worth asking directly, because it changes revision planning by several months.

The timeline that matters for tuition is simpler than the school calendar suggests. Diagnostic work belongs early in Grade 10 or late in Grade 9. Topic repair belongs in the middle. Full past-paper work under timed conditions belongs in the final ten to twelve weeks, and it does not substitute for the first two stages.

For younger students, Grade 6 to Grade 8, the request is usually different: keeping pace with a school that is already teaching in IGCSE style before the syllabus formally starts. Support runs from Grade 1 through Grade 12 depending on subject and availability.

May and November series, plus an earlier series at some centres
Diagnose early, repair in the middle, time papers in the last stretch
Grade 6 to Grade 8 support is pace-keeping, not exam prep

contentBlocks.heading: How an IGCSE tutor shortlist for Sushant Lok 3, Gurugram is put together
contentBlocks.body:
The intake conversation is short and specific. Board, subject, tier, grade, the school's current chapter, the last two marked scripts if you have them, and the two or three evening windows that genuinely work in your household. Vague answers here produce vague shortlists.

From there, tutors are filtered on subject and paper experience before anything about location. Someone who has taught Extended Chemistry across several series is a better starting point than someone nearer who last taught it once. Location filters second, timing third.

You then get a small shortlist, not a directory. Two or three profiles is the useful number, because a parent can actually read three profiles properly and cannot read thirty. Each one comes with what the tutor has taught, at what level, and in what format.

A first session follows, and it is diagnostic rather than a sales demonstration. The tutor should come out of it able to say which topics are missing, which are shaky under time, and what the first four weeks will cover in order. If they cannot say that, the match is wrong and it is better to change at week one than week six.

Changing tutors early is normal and costs less than persisting with a poor fit.
items: Board, tier, chapter position and last two marked scripts
Subject fit filtered before geography
Two or three profiles, not a browsable list
Diagnostic first session with a written four-week plan
Early swaps treated as normal, not as a complaint

contentBlocks.heading: What four weeks of IGCSE tuition should actually show you
contentBlocks.body:
No honest platform can promise a grade. What can be described is what visible progress looks like by the end of the first month, so you have something concrete to judge against instead of a feeling.

By week four you should be able to see a marked past-paper question where the child's answer is structured differently from how it was in week one: the working set out, the units carried, the command term answered rather than circled. You should see a topic list with items crossed off. And you should be able to ask your child what they are working on this fortnight and get a specific answer rather than the subject name.

What you will often not see in four weeks is the school grade moving. School assessments lag, and a child repairing a Grade 9 gap in November may score the same in December while the underlying problem is genuinely shrinking. That is the honest limitation of any short window.

If none of the three visible markers appear by week four, raise it. Either the diagnosis was wrong, the frequency is too low for the gap, or the fit is off. All three are fixable, and none of them get better by waiting another month for the situation to resolve itself.
items: A marked script that reads differently from week one
A written topic list with visible progress against it
The student can name this fortnight's focus unprompted
School grades usually lag the underlying change
No guarantees on grades, scores or improvement percentages

contentBlocks.body:
Families in and around Sushant Lok 3 commonly name Scottish High International School in Sector 57, Lancers International School on the Golf Course Road side, Pathways World School and GD Goenka World School towards the Sohna Road region. Between them these schools run different subject option blocks, different internal assessment calendars and different views on how early past papers should begin.

That matters practically. A tutor who has worked with students from a school with heavy weekly assignment loads plans differently from one used to a school that front-loads content and tests less often. Ask a prospective tutor what they have seen from students at your child's school, and listen for whether the answer is specific.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Naming them here is a description of the area families are drawn from, nothing more. No tutor is presented as a school representative, and no session content is endorsed by any school.

Where a school sets its own coursework or internal deadlines, a tutor's job is to help the student meet them honestly. Explaining a method, reviewing a draft's structure and pointing out an unsupported claim is support. Producing the work is not, and any tutor who offers it should be declined.

contentBlocks.heading: What IB Gram checks before a tutor reaches your shortlist in Gurugram
contentBlocks.body:
Verification is a process, not a badge, and it is worth stating plainly what it does and does not cover.

Identity is confirmed against a government photo identity document. Qualifications are checked against the degree or certificate claimed, and the subject of that qualification is checked against the subject the tutor wants to teach, which is where a fair number of applications stop. Teaching history is reviewed for whether the tutor has actually taught the board and tier in question, not a broadly similar course. References are followed up where a tutor claims institutional teaching experience.

A subject conversation follows. It is not a written test. A tutor is asked how they would teach a specific awkward topic, how they would mark a mediocre answer, and what they would do with a student two chapters behind six weeks before a paper. The answers separate people quickly.

What verification does not do is predict chemistry between a tutor and your child. A tutor can clear every check and still be wrong for a quiet fourteen-year-old who needs to be asked questions rather than talked at. That judgment stays with you after the first session, which is why the first session is diagnostic and why changing early is straightforward.

An advisor comes back with a short shortlist matched on subject and paper experience first, then on whether the tutor can realistically reach Sushant Lok 3 at the hour you need, or whether online is the better arrangement for that particular subject. Nothing is committed at that stage.

faqs.question: How quickly can an IGCSE tutor start sessions in Sushant Lok 3?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject and the slot. A common request such as Extended Mathematics in a 5pm to 7pm window usually moves faster than a narrow one such as Additional Mathematics at 8:30pm on weekdays only. Online matches are typically quicker than home tuition, because they are not limited by who can cross Golf Course Extension Road at that hour. Share the subject, tier and two workable windows, and an advisor can tell you what is realistically available rather than making a general promise about turnaround.

faqs.question: Is home tuition realistic inside Ireo Skyon, M3M Merlin or Emaar DigiHomes?
faqs.answer: Yes, with two caveats. Visitor registration at these towers adds a few minutes at both ends of every session, so a 60-minute booking effectively costs the tutor closer to 80. Some societies also require the resident to pre-register the visitor each time, which becomes a small weekly chore for you. Neither is a blocker. Both are worth mentioning at intake, because a tutor who knows the access routine before the first visit is less likely to arrive late and less likely to drop the slot after a month.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees depend on in this part of Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Chiefly on level, subject scarcity, format and frequency. Extended-tier science and Additional Mathematics sit higher than general Grade 8 support, because the specialist pool is smaller. Home sessions cost more than online for the same tutor, since travel time is real time. Two sessions a week is more than double the commitment of one in a tutor's calendar, so pricing is not always linear. Rates can be reviewed once the subject, tier and format are clear, and no figure quoted before that conversation would be meaningful.

faqs.question: My child is in Core Mathematics and wants to move to Extended. Can tuition help?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the honest answer depends on timing. Early in Grade 10 there is usually room to close the gap between the Core content list and the Extended one, and a tutor can work through the supplementary material systematically. Late in Grade 10 the same request becomes risky, because an unprepared candidate on the harder papers can end up below where they would have landed on Core. The decision belongs to the school, which knows the internal evidence. A tutor can prepare for the switch, not authorise it.

faqs.question: We are two months from the May papers. Is that too late to start?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but it changes what tuition can sensibly do. Two months is enough to fix answer structure, drill command terms, work through timed past papers and shore up two or three weak topics properly. It is not enough to rebuild a syllabus that was never learnt. A tutor should tell you that at the diagnostic session and pick targets accordingly, rather than attempting full coverage and finishing everything shallowly. Choosing three topics to actually secure beats skimming twelve in the time available.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry?
